question: lender_enforcement
clause: Directors and restricted employees are prohibited from dealing in Woodside securities during a black-out period (as defined in Section 4.2 below).
reasoning: Black-out periods bind only directors and restricted employees, so an ordinary employee has no closed period during which a lender's enforcement sale could breach the Policy, and the Section 7.1 exclusion for disposals resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is drafted for directors and restricted employees. question: cash_hedge
clause: Transactions involving Woodside-based derivative securities by directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan, are also prohibited.
definition: “Derivative securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights, convertible notes or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security. Transactions in derivative securities include, but are not limited to: • trading in Woodside-based option contracts; • transactions in straddles or collars; and/or • writing puts or calls.
reasoning: The Section 5 derivatives ban is not limited to unvested or locked holdings and expressly names straddles, collars and writing puts, so a cash-settled collar, put or swap is prohibited outright for the executive key management personnel and other plan executives who make up the core of this tier. A restricted employee outside that description (for example a Group General Counsel nominee who is not an executive in the incentive plan) would instead need acknowledgement under Section 6.2, which extends the Compliance Certificate requirement to third-party products limiting the economic risk of a vested holding.

question: physical_hedge

Section 6.2 operates only where the person is 'not otherwise prohibited by this Policy', so the Section 5 ban prevails.

question: borrow_against_stock
clause: Woodside securities pledged as collateral, including shares held in a margin account, may be sold without your consent by the lender in foreclosure if you default on your loan. A foreclosure sale that occurs while you are aware of inside information may, in some cases, result in unlawful insider trading. Due to this risk, directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.

A Group General Counsel nominee outside Section 8.1 would need acknowledgement under Section 6.2 because granting security is a dealing.
